headline: SWI Group, an Amsterdam-listed company building data centres in Europe and the United States, says it has raised 800 million euros from institutional investors.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score: a sizeable raise for AI data-centre buildout, but a company announcement from a little-known firm with no independent check.
importance_line: More money for data centres and the power supply they need affects the cities and grids that host them and the companies that rent the computing, but the valuation and plans are SWI's own statements.
summary: SWI Group, listed on Euronext Amsterdam, announced on 12 Oct 2026 a capital increase of 800 million euros with institutional investors at a stated valuation of 6.1 billion euros, which it says brings the equity it has raised since March 2026 to over 1 billion euros (reported also by Unite.AI). The company says the money will pay for data-centre and AI computing capacity, including power supply, in Europe and the United States, raise the share of its stock open to public trading to about 20%, and give certain investors options tied to future stock-market milestones.
notes: Source is SWI Group's own press release (PR Newswire); the pool item was a Unite.AI relay (its byline is an AI-generated research agent), also read. Status CONFIRMED reflects an official company announcement; the valuation, use of proceeds and growth plans are the company's statements.
